title: PipelineManifest
description: Output of data-pipeline. Records what was generated (modality decision, target-by-target code files, mock data, local idempotency evidence) and at what human-approval readiness level -- NOT the generated code itself, which lives on disk under output_dir. A human review gate sits between validated and any deployment; see references/toolkit-conventions.md #7. data-pipeline is the only skill of the five without a dedicated schema in the original Phase 0 set (data-contract/model-spec/quality-report/validation-report); this schema was added in Phase 2 once it became clear the run-manifest envelope alone can't carry modality/readiness/generated-file bookkeeping without redefining a shared contract every other skill also depends on. See DECISIONS.md.

pipeline_id.description: Stable identifier across re-runs for the same generated pipeline (e.g. hash of target table names), so a new run's diff can be matched to a previous one.

source_refs.description: What this pipeline was generated from. At least one of data_contract_ref / model_spec_ref must be non-null -- data-pipeline never generates code from nothing.

modality_decision.description: How this run chose among pyspark_notebook / declarative_pipeline / lakeflow_connect. Classifying the rubric_factors is interpretation (the agent's job, per toolkit-conventions.md #5); applying the rubric given those factors is deterministic (scripts/recommend_modality.py) -- confidence/basis here describes the classification step, not the rule application.

source_is_managed_connector.description: True if the source object is of a type Lakeflow Connect has a managed connector for (e.g. Salesforce, SQL Server, ServiceNow, Workday) AND no custom transformation is needed at ingestion time.

transform_complexity.description: simple_declarative: expressible as SELECT/JOIN/aggregate/MERGE with no control flow, external calls, or procedural branching. complex_procedural: needs imperative logic a declarative framework can't express.

modality_availability.description: From toolkit.yaml environment.declarative_pipelines_available / lakeflow_connect_available. pyspark_notebook is always available (the universal fallback).

merge_keys.description: Empty array only valid when load_pattern is full_refresh.

transform_spec_ref.description: Path to the portable transform spec (source-agnostic SELECT/merge-key definition) this target's code was rendered from -- kept so code can be regenerated deterministically without re-deriving the logic.

generated_as.description: e.g. 'DLT expectation: expect_or_drop' or 'not carried forward -- see assumptions'.

idempotency_check.description: Local, mock-data-based evidence that the generated merge/upsert logic is safe to re-run. This is NOT a claim the generated code was ever executed against a real Spark/Databricks target -- see references/idempotency-and-mock-data.md for exactly what is and isn't proven this way.

deployment.description: Null until a human explicitly approves, in-conversation, naming the specific target. data-pipeline itself never sets this to a non-null approved state -- see toolkit-conventions.md #1 and #7.

target_named.description: The specific job/object name the human approval named -- never a blanket approval.
